shots.text: A hundred and fifty-five million US emergency visits a year. Each one's a chain.
Before the visit, it's referrals, insurers, and a fight for a time slot.
During, it's hallways and waiting rooms. After, it's results and phone tag.
Every link is a different person. Nobody holds the whole line.
The price? About a quarter of US health spending is waste.
Doctors and their staff lose thirteen hours a week to prior auth.
And one abnormal test result in fourteen never reaches the patient.
Meet Maria. Seventy-one. Her doctor spotted something on a scan.
So Dr. Whitcombe faxes a referral to Halden Medical Center. Yes, a fax.
That fax is where Throughline grabs the thread.
Thirteen agents pass Maria's case hand to hand. People sign off at the gates.
Intake reads the fax. Smudged member ID? It asks the coordinator instead of guessing.
One answer wakes Coverage, which flags the scan and tosses it to Prior auth.
Prior auth drafts the whole request, with a source next to every line.
The coordinator approves. By hand, that's twenty-four minutes. Here, it's already written.
Scheduling takes the baton. It's a Rust engine, because schedules should be exact.
Maria's voice note says wheelchair. Messaging hears it, Itinerary reroutes around the stairs.
Visit day. One of two CT scanners is down, and nobody's said a word.
Waiting-room sensing counts heads in the camera frames and sees the line swell.
It hands the problem straight to the Ops planner.
The planner plays out the next ninety minutes twenty different ways.
Best fix? Average CT wait drops from seventeen minutes to five.
The operations lead approves. Seven patients re-planned, and every phone gets the why.
Once Maria's home, Discharge puts the doctor's notes in plain words, and the doctor signs off.
Still unsure the next day? Discharge hands her to a nurse.
Results watch guards her test. Follow-up books the next visit and closes the loop.
Muse Spark reads and drafts. Voice Transcribe listens. SAM counts.
The planner runs on Muse Spark Open, open weights, on Baseten.
And it's not one hospital. Northgate alone: five buildings, a fourteen-floor tower.
Nobody had to hold Maria's thread.
This time, Throughline held it.
